body.statement: Uniformly over \(\theta\in[-K,K]\), \(\sqrt{n_1t_1}(\widehat{\operatorname{ATT}}_M-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})/\widehat\sigma_M\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), \(\widehat\sigma_M\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), and \(\inf_{\theta\in[-K,K]}\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_M\}\to1-\alpha\). In addition, \((n_1t_1)^{-1}\sum_{i:d_i=1}\sum_{t:qvec_t=1}\widehat L_{M,it}=o_p((n_1t_1)^{-1/2})\) uniformly.
body.justification: As an internal control, masking removes the heterogeneous treatment factor from every training cell, so uniformity spans the bounded absorption transition.
body.gap: Bai and Ng (2021) give pointwise block-imputation normality, not this compact-amplitude result paired with full-sample absorption.
body.consumer: It supplies an internal benchmark showing that the full-sample failure is caused by fitting the treated-post spike rather than by the Gaussian oracle experiment itself.
